synopsis: Safety Integrity Level denotes the IEC 61508 safety-function grades SIL 1–4, not software-in-the-loop; context distinguishes reliability requirements from test methods, where the booklet recommends software-in-the-loop for volume and hardware-in-the-loop for timing, interfaces and faults [f12048, f12050, f12058, f12057, f13341]. For frequently acting functions, SIL specifies dangerous-failure probability bands: SIL 1 spans one failure in 100,000 to one million hours, each higher grade is ten times stricter, and SIL 3 spans 10^-8–10^-7 per hour and is roughly as demanding as PL e [f12051, f12052]. The grade also governs hardware-analysis and software-development rigor, while FMEDA supplies failure classifications for diagnostic coverage and PL, MPL and SIL probability calculations [f12053, f12098]. Chapter 9 requires the collision-mitigation intervention path to receive a performance-level or integrity assignment plus fault testing, consistent with the glossary requirement and mining customers’ safety-integrity specifications [f7455, f15273, f12059]. Standards selection remains unresolved: IEC 61508, IEC 62061 and ISO 25119 are listed as alternatives whose fit was not verified, Chapter 9’s editions were not verified, and IEC 62061:2021 is listed as current but not reviewed [f12054, f7455, f15267].
